post_title: Generating PDFs in Python is a nightmare
post_content: I have been fighting with ReportLab and WeasyPrint for 3 days. We just need to generate customized invoices and compliance reports from our database, but keeping the formatting from breaking when tables span multiple pages is impossible. Is there a modern way to do this?

post_title: Ask HN: Best tool for programmatic DOCX generation?
post_content: We need to auto-generate NDAs and Master Service Agreements where our users just fill in a form and we spit out a perfectly formatted Word document. python-docx is too low level. What are people using in 2026?

post_title: How to reliably convert markdown to PDF with complex tables?
post_content: We have an automated pipeline that generates reports in Markdown, but when we convert them to PDF using pandoc, the tables always break or get cut off. We need a way to reliably generate pixel-perfect PDFs from our data.

post_title: Tired of puppeteer for PDF generation
post_content: We are currently spinning up a headless Chrome instance via Puppeteer just to take a 'screenshot' of an HTML page to generate our PDFs. It's incredibly slow, uses way too much memory, and the pagination is unpredictable. Anyone have a better architecture for this?

post_title: Feature Request: Export to properly formatted DOCX
post_content: It would be great if this tool could export the final analysis not just as a raw text dump, but as a properly formatted Word document with headers and footers intact. Right now my users have to copy-paste the output into their company templates manually.
